components.name: Primary Button
components.description: High-emphasis action. One per screen. Near-white fill in dark mode.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; background: oklch(0.922 0 0); color: oklch(0.205 0 0); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease; white-space: nowrap; outline: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.922 0 0 / 0.8); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.556 0 0 / 0.5); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action. Border at rest; muted fill on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.985 0 0); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid oklch(1 0 0 / 0.1); border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; white-space: nowrap; outline: none; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: oklch(0.269 0 0); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.556 0 0 / 0.5); }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Standard form input. Transparent background, border, md radius. Focus ring is the only depth effect.
components.css: .ds-input { display: block; width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; background: oklch(1 0 0 / 0); color: oklch(0.985 0 0); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; border: 1px solid oklch(1 0 0 / 0.15); border-radius: 8px; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.556 0 0); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: oklch(0.556 0 0); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.556 0 0 / 0.5); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

narrative.overview:
Air IDE operates at the intersection of radical restraint and precise signal. The interface is a controlled absence: near-black surfaces recede deliberately so that code — and only code — commands attention. This is not minimalism as aesthetic fashion; it is a functional discipline. Every pixel of chrome that goes dark is one fewer distraction from the task at hand.

Where colour appears, it carries weight. The electric-blue/violet accent family is reserved exclusively for live connection state, the loading animation, the brand mark glyph, and the 'IDE' wordmark. It is never used for decoration. Its rarity is the point: when you see blue, the system is telling you something is alive and networked.

The achromatic main UI is strict. Surfaces separate not by shadow but by lightness step. The typography is Figtree Variable: warm-geometric, rounded, and confident without being expressive. In the editor and any code-mode context, JetBrains Mono carries ligatures and a tight mono rhythm.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black environment; code is the visual subject, chrome is the frame
Colour = signal only; the signal accent appears ≤10% of any given screen
Tonal separation without shadow; no box-shadows in the main UI at rest
Two-font system: Figtree for UI chrome, monospace for code/terminal contexts
Developer-terse copy: 'Live' not 'You're connected', 'L12 · C4' not 'cursor at line 12'
Backdrop-blur headers and glassmorphic terminal card are the only allowed depth effects

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The electric-blue accent and its gradient siblings are reserved for live-connection signaling and brand marks. Do not apply them to buttons, borders, focus rings, or informational UI. The moment blue appears as a general accent it loses its meaning.

rules.name: The No-Chroma-in-Chrome Rule
rules.body: All surface, border, and text tokens carry zero chroma. Introducing any tinted neutral breaks the void and draws attention away from code.

rules.name: The Two-Zone Rule
rules.body: Figtree and mono never appear in the same text run. UI chrome is Figtree. Code context, invite codes, and terminal-flavoured UI are mono.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on cards, panels, dialogs, or buttons in the running app. Depth comes from tonal lightness difference alone. Blur is allowed only on header overlays; glow is allowed only in the loading screen.

rules.name: The Graduated Corner Rule
rules.body: Corner size scales with surface importance: pill for dots and badges, md for interactive controls, xl for content cards. Never mix a square control with a rounded card in the same layer.

dos: Do use oklch() values directly when writing custom inline styles — the project's source of truth is OKLCH.
Do use bg-card/90 backdrop-blur-md for all sticky headers that need to feel elevated without a shadow.
Do use the mono font stack ('JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Cascadia Code', monospace) for invite codes, file names in the status bar, and any terminal-idiom text.
Do add font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-xs text-muted-foreground to sidebar section labels.
Do prefer hover:bg-muted over custom hover backgrounds for interactive rows.
Do use ring-1 ring-foreground/10 as the card border substitute — never add a border property to Card components.
Do keep the signal accent (oklch(0.65 0.22 264) and family) exclusively for live-connection and brand-glyph contexts.
Do represent status semantically: emerald for live, amber for connecting, red for error — and only for those states.
donts: Don't add box-shadow to cards, panels, buttons, or dialogs in the main running UI. Shadows belong only in the loading screen.
Don't use the signal-blue family for focus rings, hover highlights, or decorative accents.
Don't introduce a tinted neutral surface — all surfaces are achromatic; chroma = zero outside the signal family.
Don't use colour for decorative hierarchy; use border-b border-border or a lightness-step surface instead.
Don't use the card component for the loading screen — it has its own bespoke glassmorphic terminal card.
Don't inline a tighter or looser font than text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider for sidebar section headers.
Don't add a full colour fill to the destructive button variant — keep it bg-destructive/10.
